title: In Ezra 5 In What Ways Can Remembering Gods Past Faithfulness Encourage Us In Our Current Challenges
paragraphs: Remembering God’s Past Faithfulness: Encouragement from Ezra 5

The book of Ezra captures a pivotal moment in Israel’s history, focusing on the return from Babylonian exile and the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem. Ezra 5, in particular, highlights how the people overcame significant opposition by recalling God’s faithfulness and responding in obedience and courage. Let’s explore how remembering God’s past acts can embolden us to face present challenges.
The Historical Setting of Ezra 5

After years of exile, the Israelites returned to Jerusalem to reconstruct the temple. However, their progress was halted by adversaries and royal decrees. Years passed, and discouragement set in. But in Ezra 5, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah called the people to resume the work:

Then the prophets, Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied unto the Jews that were in Judah and Jerusalem; in the name of the God of Israel prophesied they unto them. - Ezra 5:1 ASV
Their encouragement was rooted not only in God’s word for the present but in His unchanging character and previous acts of deliverance.
How Remembering God’s Faithfulness Helped Them
Renewed Courage to Obey
The leaders and people resumed building, even though opposition remained:

But the eye of their God was upon the elders of the Jews, and they could not cause them to cease, till the matter should come to Darius, and then answer should be returned by letter concerning it. - Ezra 5:5 ASV

Their confidence was not in their own strength, but in the assurance that God was watching over them—as He had done for their ancestors. This remembrance gave them courage to obey God despite threats.
Confidence in God’s Sovereignty

When challenged by Persian officials, the Jews answered by recounting their history—God’s dealings with them, the reason for the exile, and the favor God had shown through Cyrus’ decree (Ezra 5:11-13 ASV). Their response reflected a deep trust in God’s sovereign hand guiding both their past and present.
Encouragement from Prophecy and Promises
The prophets Haggai and Zechariah did more than urge the people onward; they reminded them of God’s promises. For example:

Yet now be strong, O Zerubbabel, saith Jehovah; and be strong, O Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and be strong, all ye people of the land, saith Jehovah, and work: for I am with you, saith Jehovah of hosts. - Haggai 2:4 ASV
The assurance of God’s presence, rooted in His faithfulness, emboldened them to persevere.
Applying These Truths to Our Lives
Just as the Israelites were strengthened by recalling God’s past acts, so too can we find hope and courage. Here’s how:
Reflect on Personal and Biblical History
Remember occasions when God has answered prayers, provided for needs, or delivered from trouble. Scripture is full of such reminders:
Bless Jehovah, O my soul, And forget not all his benefits: - Psalms 103:2 ASV
Rest in God’s Unchanging Character
God’s faithfulness is foundational to our faith:
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and to-day, yea and for ever. - Hebrews 13:8 ASV
Move Forward in Faith
Even when circumstances are difficult, remembering what God has already done gives us courage to step out in obedience:
For we walk by faith, not by sight. - 2 Corinthians 5:7 ASV
Conclusion

Ezra 5 teaches that recalling God’s faithfulness in the past is a powerful antidote to discouragement and fear. When we remember how God has acted before—both in Scripture and in our own lives—we are emboldened to trust Him with our present challenges. His character has not changed, and His promises remain sure.
